topic: How do vaccines train the immune system?
narration: A vaccine gives you a safe practice round. Say, just one harmless spike from the virus, that can't multiply. Patrol cells grab it and flash its mugshot to your lymph nodes. A matching B cell wakes up and clones itself thousands of times. Those clones pump out Y shaped antibodies that stick to the spike and block it. When the drill ends, most clones die off. But a handful stay as memory cells, on guard for years.
